title: Unified Inventory Forecasting for Global Retail
business: Global retail enterprises managing fragmented supply chain data across disparate regional warehouses.
problem: Data silos between regional inventory databases and central demand planning systems prevent accurate, real-time stock replenishment, leading to frequent stockouts and overstocking.
solution: Utilize the Databricks Lakehouse platform to ingest raw regional inventory logs into a unified Delta Lake architecture, enabling collaborative data engineering and machine learning model development on a single source of truth.
steps: Configure Unity Catalog to centralize access control and define metadata schemas for regional inventory datasets.
Develop ETL pipelines using Databricks notebooks to ingest and clean raw inventory logs into bronze, silver, and gold Delta tables.
Train demand forecasting models using MLflow to track experiments and model versions across global regions.
Deploy the final model as a SQL-accessible function within Databricks SQL for real-time inventory replenishment dashboards.
outcome: A unified view of global inventory levels that allows supply chain managers to execute data-driven replenishment strategies without moving data between isolated systems.
limitation: The platform relies on the consistency of the underlying cloud object storage; users must monitor storage latency and throughput limits to ensure that high-frequency ingestion does not degrade query performance for downstream BI dashboards.

code.content:
# Read raw inventory data from cloud storage
df = spark.read.format("delta").load("/mnt/inventory/raw")
# Clean and write to silver table for downstream consumption
df.filter("stock_level >= 0").write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save("/mnt/inventory/silver")
code.explanation: This code demonstrates the ingestion process where raw inventory logs are filtered and persisted into a Delta table, serving as the foundation for the unified inventory view.
